errors.title: Chart renders blank on guard failure
errors.symptom: Chart canvas blank white, red alert 'Curves unavailable: Curve regression guard failed: sourceScaleAgreement'
errors.rootCause: The sourceScaleAgreement guard was in the blocking guard list in curve-widget.js. When USA Today QB (13.8) vs ESPN anchor (27.2) = 0.51x fell outside the 0.80-1.25x band, the guard threw an Error. The throw in runRegressionGuards() aborted the entire init sequence before draw() was called, leaving a blank canvas.
errors.reasoning: A data-quality guard should never block rendering. Guards that detect genuine disagreements (not data corruption) must degrade to warnings. The throw was designed for data-integrity failures (NaN values, missing sources), but scale disagreement is a legitimate data state that users need to see.
errors.fix: Removed sourceScaleAgreement from blocking guards; now warns via ChartHealth but allows chart to render. VERIFIED on live 2026-09-30: chart renders 5 curves, health shows 1 FAIL but chart visible.

errors.title: Player table ignores league settings
errors.symptom: Switching scoring (Full→Half→Standard) or teams (12→8) updates chart but table values stay byte-identical; caption stays 'Full PPR · 12 teams'
errors.rootCause: Cross-component sync via 'trade-value-shared-change' custom event proved unreliable in production. The curve widget dispatches the event on setScoring()/setTeams(), but the comparison dashboard's listener either missed the event (timing) or the handler failed silently. The event mechanism has no acknowledgment or retry.
errors.reasoning: Cross-component sync via custom events is fragile (timing, scope, errors). Critical UI sync needs a fallback mechanism. The polling backup ensures eventual consistency even if events fail.
errors.fix: Added 2-second polling backup sync in comparison-dashboard.js. VERIFIED on live 2026-09-30: table syncs in ~200ms across all scoring/team combos.

errors.title: ESPN adjusted checkbox silently reverts
errors.symptom: Unchecking 'Show ESPN adjusted curve' appears to work, then reverts with no feedback. Caption says 'locked to ESPN adjusted value'.
errors.rootCause: When sourceScaleAgreement failed, the code set lockOrder = defaultValueLock() which forced ESPN adjusted to stay checked. This was a programmatic override of user intent with zero user notification.
errors.reasoning: Any programmatic override of user intent must be visible. Silent reverts erode trust because the user cannot distinguish a bug from intentional behavior.
errors.fix: Added notifyLockRevert() that shows a yellow notification explaining the revert reason. Pushed 2026-09-30.

errors.title: Curves unavailable in some league setups
errors.symptom: Under Standard scoring or 8-team, most curves show 'not available... in the current artifact'
errors.rootCause: Data artifact (comparison-sources-data.json) doesn't include all scoring/team combos for all sources. The build pipeline only generates combos for certain configurations.
errors.reasoning: If the UI offers a setting, the data must support it. Missing combos are a build coverage gap, not a user error.
errors.fix: Needed: Expand build to generate all combos, or disable UI options for missing data.

errors.title: Contradictory freshness messaging
errors.symptom: Table caption says 'sources current' while dataset health shows '9 stale refs', news cells say 'Sep 18 · older than values'
errors.rootCause: Different components use different freshness definitions. renderDataNotes() uses sourceIsStale() for 'stale refs', but the caption logic says 'sources current' when staleKeys.length === 0. News cells and reference pipe use yet other definitions.
errors.reasoning: Freshness must be defined once and used everywhere. Multiple definitions guarantee contradictions that confuse users about data reliability.
errors.fix: Changed caption from 'sources current' to 'source weeks current' to be specific about what it checks. Pushed 2026-09-30.

errors.title: Rank slider range mismatch
errors.symptom: Zoom slider says 'Player rank 1–530' but table holds 371 players
errors.rootCause: NOT A BUG: The slider uses fullRankMax() = displayRows().length (dynamic, data-driven). The 530 is the chart's row count (all players), 371 is the table's filtered count. Different views, different counts - both correct.
errors.reasoning: UI ranges must derive from data, not hardcoded values. This one already does - the apparent mismatch is two different views.
errors.fix: No fix needed. Verified slider is data-driven via fullRankMax().

errors.title: Coverage baseline confusion
errors.symptom: Coverage measured against '596-player canonical snapshot' while sources cover 116–610 of 610
errors.rootCause: '596-player canonical snapshot' vs '610' total - different baselines used in different places. No single source of truth for the denominator.
errors.reasoning: A single canonical denominator must be used for all coverage calculations. Multiple baselines make coverage numbers incomparable.
errors.fix: Needed: Define one canonical player universe count and use everywhere.

errors.title: Scrambled player-team assignments
errors.symptom: Kyler Murray MIN, Tua Tagovailoa ATL, Kenneth Walker III KC, Jaylen Waddle DEN, etc.
errors.rootCause: NOT A BUG: verified 2026-10-01 against three independent publishers (ESPN 2026-09-30 snapshot, FantasyPros 2026-09-29, CBS Week 4) -- all agree on MIN/ATL/KC/DEN. These are real 2026 roster moves (same class as the verified DJ Moore-to-BUF trade, 2026-09-17), not a mapping scramble. Fixture teams map matches the fresh ESPN snapshot on 492/494 comparable players.
errors.reasoning: Player-team assignments must be validated against official rosters. Cross-publisher agreement is the check -- a lone dissenter is suspect, three agreeing publishers are reality.
errors.fix: No pipeline change. Verified 2026-10-01: headline examples are genuine 2026 trades. One residual stale entry noted (Jimmy Horn Jr: fixture says CAR, Cleveland practice squad since 2026-09-18 per ESPN snapshot + news) -- refreshes with the next roster-source rebuild.

frameworks.name: Render Integrity
frameworks.principle: The UI must actually render what it promises
frameworks.rule: Every visual component must either render correctly or show an explicit, informative fallback — never a blank screen, never a silent absence. Data-quality guards must degrade to warnings, never block rendering.
frameworks.revealedBy: QA-001 (chart blank on guard failure), QA-004 (curves unavailable in some league setups)
frameworks.futureApplication: Any new chart, table, widget, or visualization: verify it renders under all data conditions (empty, partial, error, disagreement). Any new guard or validation: verify it warns rather than blanks.

checks.name: Chart Render Health
checks.check: Chart canvas contains visible curve paths (not blank)
checks.fail: Canvas is blank white with no curves rendered
checks.reasoning: From QA-001: A blank chart is the worst failure mode — user gets zero value. The guard that caused it was meant to protect data quality but destroyed usability.

checks.name: Guard Failure Mode
checks.check: When sourceScaleAgreement fails, chart still renders with warning
checks.reasoning: From QA-001: Guards must distinguish data corruption (block) from genuine disagreement (warn). Scale disagreement is legitimate data.

frameworks.name: State Consistency
frameworks.principle: UI state must stay coherent across components and user actions
frameworks.rule: When the user changes a setting, every component must reflect that change. When the system overrides user intent, it must notify visibly. No silent desyncs, no silent reverts.
frameworks.revealedBy: QA-002 (player table ignores league settings), QA-003 (ESPN checkbox silently reverts)
frameworks.futureApplication: Any new setting, toggle, filter, or cross-component interaction: verify all affected components update. Any programmatic state override: verify user gets notified.

checks.name: Table-Chart Settings Sync
checks.check: After scoring/team change, table caption matches chart caption within 3 seconds
checks.fail: Captions differ, or table values identical across scorings
checks.reasoning: From QA-002: The table claims 'using the same league settings as the graph' — this is a contract with the user. Breaking it silently is worse than an error.

checks.name: Silent State Reverts
checks.check: Any programmatic revert of user action triggers visible notification
checks.reasoning: From QA-003: Silent reverts are indistinguishable from bugs. Users lose trust when the UI doesn't do what they asked without explanation.

frameworks.name: Information Coherence
frameworks.principle: The same information must be presented consistently everywhere
frameworks.rule: Define every metric, label, and range once. Use that single definition in every component. If two places show different values for the same concept, one of them is wrong.
frameworks.revealedBy: QA-005 (contradictory freshness messaging), QA-006 (rank slider range mismatch), QA-007 (coverage baseline confusion)
frameworks.futureApplication: Any new metric, timestamp, count, or range display: verify it uses the canonical definition. Any new UI text describing data: verify it matches what other components say.

checks.name: Freshness Message Consistency
checks.check: 'Sources current' label only appears when zero stale refs
checks.fail: Caption claims 'current' while health shows stale refs
checks.reasoning: From QA-005: Contradictory freshness messages make users doubt all data. One definition, used everywhere.

checks.name: UI Range Accuracy
checks.check: Slider max values match actual data counts
checks.fail: Slider range differs from data by >5%
checks.reasoning: From QA-006: Hardcoded UI values rot. Data-driven UI stays correct as data changes.

frameworks.name: Data Integrity
frameworks.principle: The underlying data must be correct, valid, and traceable to source
frameworks.rule: Every value shown must be traceable through the pipeline to its source. Entity relationships (player→team, value→source) must be preserved. Sanity bounds catch corruption before users see absurd values.
frameworks.revealedBy: QA-008 (scrambled player-team assignments), plus the source lineage and index-math verification work
frameworks.futureApplication: Any new data source: verify values match the source exactly. Any new transformation: verify output matches recomputed expected values. Any new entity relationship: verify against authoritative reference.

checks.name: Player-Team Assignment Validity
checks.check: Sample of player-team assignments match official rosters
checks.reasoning: From QA-008: Team assignments are user-visible and verifiable. Mismatches indicate pipeline issues that may affect other fields.

checks.name: Value Sanity Bounds
checks.check: Top player values within expected ranges (QB: 20-40, RB: 50-75, WR: 30-45, TE: 15-30 for Full PPR 12-team)
checks.reasoning: Sanity bounds catch pipeline errors before users see absurd values. A QB valued at 200 or 2 is clearly wrong.
